parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Today, we’re starting a series of lectures on ethics in engineering, that is, engineering principles relating to right and wrong conduct, and the sorts of moral responsibilities that you will have to uphold in your professional lives. I’m going to start by giving you a brief outline of the history of ethics in engineering. It was, of course, only in the nineteenth century that engineering really emerged as a profession. Initially, ethical issues were considered to be a personal matter, something to be decided in accordance with one’s own principles and values. However, things gradually changed as the profession grew, and as engineering projects became larger and more complex. A need began to be felt for a more codified set of principles that all engineers would agree to follow.

Unfortunately, it took three major disasters to bring about this change in attitude. All three of these involved the collapse of bridges. The first, known as the Ashtabula River Railroad disaster, happened in 1876 in the USA, and we now think it was probably caused by metal fatigue. Then in 1879 there was a second disaster, this time in Scotland. This occurred because engineers had failed to correctly calculate the effects that wind would have on the structure. The third collapse occurred in 1907 in Canada. This was also due to an engineering design problem. The weight of the structure was so great that it could not support itself, and it collapsed. Public outcry over disasters such as these eventually led to the establishment of professional societies for engineers in most industrializing societies. Another different type of disaster also had an impact on the development of professional engineering organizations, and I’d like to talk about this in a little more detail.

This incident, which happened early in the 20th century, is known as the Boston Molasses disaster. At the time molasses was used rather than sugar as the principal sweetener in the USA. It was also used in the manufacture of a number of other important products. One company in the city of Boston had a large amount of molasses waiting to be transferred to another factory. The molasses, more than 8 million liters of thick sticky liquid, was stored in a tank. Suddenly, this collapsed, unleashing a wave of molasses up to 5 meters high. Nearby buildings were swept off their foundations and crashed to the ground. The wave also swept away a considerable stretch of railway track. Many streets round the factory were covered with a thick layer of sticky brown molasses.

Local residents were furious as they felt that the company was to blame. They banded together and succeeded in bringing about a trial, charging the company with negligence. After three years, the company was found responsible for the accident and required to pay out in damages the equivalent of six or seven million dollars in today’s money. Even today no one is absolutely sure about the immediate causes of the accident.

However, it is certainly clear that not enough safety tests were carried out. Had these been done in accordance with the standards now applicable, then the accident would almost certainly have been prevented. It seems that the collapse was probably brought about by fermentation of the molasses, which led to an increase in pressure. This increase probably exerted too much force against a fatigue crack or some other weakness. However, this was one of the main incidents which led to increased legislation in the 1920s to regulate engineers and the engineering profession. It is the reason why we can now only operate if we have gained a license. This requires us always to be conscientious about doing everything necessary to avoid disasters, however time-consuming or expensive this may sometimes seem.

analyses.content: 利用时间状语 At first 定位到录音中的 Initially，紧接着听到伦理问题被视为 personal matter（个人私事），直接填入。
Initially, ethical issues were considered to be a personal matter, something to be decided in accordance with one’s own principles and values.
你可能想填 principles 或 values，但原文说的是根据这些原则和价值观来决定“个人私事”，不要填错对象。
定位到 1879 - Scotland，录音中提到工程师没有计算好 wind（风）对结构的影响，对应题干中的 impact of...。
Unfortunately, it took three major disasters to bring about this change in attitude. All three of these involved the collapse of bridges.
听到 three disasters（三次灾难）时就要警觉，随后录音明确说这三次都涉及 bridges（桥梁）的坍塌。
Then in 1879 there was a second disaster, this time in Scotland. This occurred because engineers had failed to correctly calculate the effects that wind would have on the structure.
注意 effects 和 impact 的同义替换，不要因为听到 structure 就走神，答案就在它前面。
定位到 1879 - Scotland，录音中提到工程师没有计算好 wind（风）对结构的影响，对应题干中的 impact of...。
The third collapse occurred in 1907 in Canada. This was also due to an engineering design problem. The weight of the structure was so great that it could not support itself, and it collapsed.
定位到 1907 - Canada，录音说结构的 weight（重量）太大导致无法支撑自己，对应题干 support its own...。
At the time molasses was used rather than sugar as the principal sweetener in the USA.
千万别填 sugar，原文说的是 rather than sugar（而不是糖），这是典型的否定干扰。
听到话题转换到 Boston Molasses Disaster，录音说糖蜜（molasses）是当时的 principal（主要的）sweetener（甜味剂），对应题干的 main。
The molasses, more than 8 million liters of thick sticky liquid, was stored in a tank. Suddenly, this collapsed, unleashing a wave of molasses up to 5 meters high.
题干问是什么东西的 collapse（倒塌），录音中提到糖蜜存储在 tank（储罐）里，然后 Suddenly, this collapsed，答案即为 tank。
Local residents were furious as they felt that the company was to blame. They banded together and succeeded in bringing about a trial, charging the company with negligence.
不要填 negligence（疏忽），这是控告公司的罪名，而不是居民要求举行的活动（审判）。
题干说当地居民 insisted on（坚持要/促成了）什么，录音中说居民团结起来 succeeded in bringing about a trial（成功促成了一场审判）。
However, it is certainly clear that not enough safety tests were carried out.
题干也是找原因，关键词是 checks（检查），录音中说 not enough safety tests（不够多的安全测试），tests 对应 checks，答案是 safety。
It seems that the collapse was probably brought about by fermentation of the molasses, which led to an increase in pressure.
录音提到 fermentation（发酵）导致了 increase in pressure（压力的增加），对应题干 raised the...。

However, this was one of the main incidents which led to increased legislation in the 1920s to regulate engineers and the engineering profession. It is the reason why we can now only operate if we have gained a license.
注意拼写，英式 licence 和美式 license 都是对的，但不要写成 legislation，那是法律法规，是导致需要执照的原因。
题干说现在这对工程师是 obligatory（强制的/必须的），录音说如果不 gained a license（获得执照）就不能执业（only operate if...）。
